task: Save a reusable checklist and then save this project's current answers.
evidence_type: Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.
facts: The page has a 'Reusable checklist' panel and a 'Project answers' panel, each with a button labelled 'Save'.
Panel headings and borders are visible at the tested desktop width. A narrow layout retains both headings but separates the project heading from its Save button by a long answer list.
A supplied synthetic trace shows the first Save updates only checklist questions; the second updates only project answers. Both changes persist after refresh.
An editor may save project answers. Only an owner may alter the reusable checklist. The tested account is owner.
No evidence records someone choosing the wrong Save. No mobile interaction trace or human observations are available.

task: Submit a valid appointment request and determine whether it was received.
evidence_type: Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.
facts: After Submit, the UI shows a spinner for 20 seconds and then returns to the enabled form without a message.
The synthetic automation trace reports a network interception timeout. There is no application response body or server record available.
A second supplied trace with interception disabled reaches a receipt screen, but uses a different date and browser session.
No retry was made for the first request because submission status was uncertain. The fixture allows read-only status lookup when a request ID is available; the first trace contains no request ID.
Only the supplied traces are authorized in this review; server access and further submissions are unavailable.

task: Permanently delete an obsolete workspace while retaining another workspace.
evidence_type: Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.
facts: Delete opens a dialog naming the workspace and stating that all its records will be permanently deleted and cannot be restored.
The dialog requires entering the workspace name before Delete enables. Cancel closes it without changing data.
A synthetic trace confirms the named workspace is deleted and the other workspace remains unchanged.
The stated product requirement requires explicit confirmation for irreversible workspace deletion.
No evidence shows incorrect names, failed cancellation, inaccessible controls or unintended deletion. A stakeholder requests removing the dialog because it adds a step.

task: Start a new note from a saved template without writing from scratch.
evidence_type: Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.
facts: A large blank editor fills most of the initial viewport. A template gallery appears below it.
Immediately above the editor, a visible button reads 'Use a saved template' and includes the shortcut Ctrl+T.
The supplied keyboard trace shows the button in focus order with the same accessible name; activating it opens the gallery and returns focus to the selected template preview.
Selecting a template populates the editor without overwriting an existing note; the starting editor is empty.
No human discoverability study, narrow-viewport trace or screen-reader test is supplied.

task: Compare two export presets, then continue editing the current draft.
evidence_type: Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.
facts: The preset list displays names but no size or format details. Details appear only after selecting Apply.
Applying a preset changes export settings and replaces the unsaved draft title with the preset name.
In two supplied synthetic traces, returning to the previous preset restores its settings but does not restore the draft title. Undo is disabled after preset application.
A saved draft copy retains the previous title; saving before comparison is a working workaround.
The stated task permits comparison without committing an export. No evidence establishes whether the title replacement is intended. Actual export submission was not performed.

task: Set an animation duration to roughly eight seconds while retaining frame-accurate control.
evidence_type: Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.
facts: The duration field accepts a positive integer labelled 'Frames'. A separate settings panel shows the current frame rate as 24 fps.
A supplied synthetic trace enters 192 frames and the preview lasts eight seconds. Changing to 30 fps while leaving 192 frames produces 6.4 seconds.
The interface does not show seconds next to Frames or explain whether duration will remain constant after a frame-rate change.
The stated professional workflow requires exact frame counts and permits changing frame rate. It does not specify which quantity should be preserved automatically.
No human timing, comprehension or error-rate measurements exist.
